dedupe_keys.name: power flexible ai data centres grid responsive compute demonstrated on a 130 kw gpu cluster arxiv 2026

description: This article explores how GPU-based AI data centres can act as grid-interactive assets, not inflexible peak loads, which traditional planning treats as causing costly upgrades and long interconnection delays. It describes an architecture that integrates grid signals, workload scheduling and power telemetry for fine-grained cluster power control. Experimental results from a real-world deployment on a 130 kW GPU cluster show rapid load reduction, sustained curtailment and carbon-aware operation with service levels kept for priority jobs, and performance-aware load shifting across geographically distributed clusters so workloads move toward regions with lower grid stress. Producer: a team of 18 authors including Chris Williams, Philip Colangelo and Ayse Coskun, submitted 23 June 2026. Coverage: one cluster and multi-cluster shifting, not a grid-wide result. Access: free arXiv preprint; only the abstract page was read, and no data release was confirmed. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: a small cluster demonstration whose numbers were not read, and authors' affiliations were not checked. Simulation uses: the demonstrated response ranges give parameters for capacity-planning and operations models that treat data centres as flexible loads. Related record: the AI data centre flexibility grid capacity expansion model (model-ai-data-centre-flexibility-grid-capacity-expansion-defer-shift).
